SYNTHETIC LEARNER PROFILE — N-482
Age: 9

CURRENT — teacher-confirmed communication and access
Uses spontaneous spoken phrases of 2–5 words and a 2-by-3 AAC grid with Break, Help,
Finished, More, Yes, and No. Speech and AAC are equally valid. Do not require verbal
repetition after successful AAC. Pointing is valid. Wait at least five seconds. Pushing
materials away or saying no may communicate refusal, not noncompliance.

CURRENT — learning and access
Follows brief concrete one-step directions. Two-step directions need visual sequencing.
Matching, sorting, sequencing, route colors, station icons, and transit symbols are
strengths. Use a short model followed by immediate practice; long verbal explanations
are ineffective. Engagement is 6–8 minutes; teaching blocks must be six minutes or less
with a visible endpoint. Avoid crowded worksheets and use no more than four high-contrast,
low-clutter response options. No sound effects, applause, alarms, or audio prompts. Use
calm speech and visuals, blue organizing accents, literal neutral images, and large touch
targets. Do not require handwriting or cutting. Allow pointing, card placement, stamping,
or AAC. Avoid exaggerated red angry-face graphics.

CURRENT — interests and reinforcement
Subway maps, city bus route maps, blue transit lines, station symbols, route matching,
and arranging stops in order. A meaningful reinforcer is two minutes tracing or building
a route on a transit map. Use a five-token board with bus-icon tokens. Picture and name
the selected reward. Effective praise: “You asked for a break by yourself.”

CURRENT — transitions, prompting, and generalization
The hardest transition is a preferred transit activity to table or paper work. Use a
First–Then board, one-minute visual warning, functional two-minute break, visible timer,
and show First–Then again on return. Honor a valid break when feasible. Do not provoke
distress or frame leaving as defiance; begin with low-pressure role-play. Prompt sequence:
independent opportunity, visual or gestural cue, model, brief verbal prompt. Never use
hand-over-hand prompting. Use “Let us try it together.” Fade promptly. Generalize across
transit-map to table work, art to cleanup, and free choice to shared reading.

HISTORICAL: Dinosaurs are no longer motivating.
NOT APPROVED: Food rewards. Tablet or video as a default reinforcer.
NOT MEANINGFUL: Generic stars without a pictured reward.
UNCONFIRMED: Paired Spanish labels; photographs versus line drawings; same break routine in every setting.
OMITTED: Medical history, medication, family contacts, school, provider, and location.
